summary: Change tries to preserve input dtypes on pandas output but is fundamentally broken: it references an undefined `dtypes` variable in the default branch (NameError) and unconditionally forces output back to input dtypes, corrupting transformers that modify values. Not mergeable.

issues.description: In `_wrap_data_with_container`, the added `if dtypes is not None:` block references `dtypes`, which is never defined/assigned in that function scope. This raises `NameError` on the default (non-pandas) output path, breaking every estimator not configured for pandas output.

Unconditional `data_to_wrap.astype(dtypes)` using `original_input.dtypes` is a correctness regression for transformers that MODIFY values. E.g. StandardScaler/normalizers on an int column produce floats that get cast back to int (feature_names_out match original names), silently truncating/corrupting data. Dtype preservation must be opt-in and only when values are unchanged.

Feature is applied always rather than gated behind a config flag as the issue itself requested ('optionally preserve'). No mechanism to enable/disable; also fails when output columns differ from input (feature selection drops columns, transformers add columns) since dtypes is keyed by original column names.
New `dtypes` parameter of `_wrap_in_pandas_container` has no docstring entry describing it.
Stray blank line inserted at the very top of the file (before `from functools import wraps`); unrelated formatting noise.
